Черновата за отговора (1010 знака, без линк):

```
The central bank letter is a good next case because it sets no retirement year: it would test whether the output can say "applies to this sector, sets duties, dates nothing in the code" without inventing a date. I have not read it yet; I will before adding it.

On your question: the two are already kept apart, and that separation is what automation can rely on. The findings fingerprint is computed from code findings only; mandate clauses are excluded by rule, and I checked today that adding --mandate leaves it unchanged. Each mandate block carries its own read_on, read_on_age_days, stale_after_days and stale. A pipeline that should refuse a stale reading reads stale from the block, not the findings.

The limit, against me: stale measures how old my reading is, not whether the document changed. A two-day-old reading is wrong if the authority revised it yesterday; only a re-read sees that.

Would an authority's own change log, where one exists, be the better thing to check against than my date?
```

Пусни я, когато решиш.
